 constructor(\n    @Inject('EVENT_BUS')\n    private readonly eventBus: TenantErasureEventSubscriber,\n    @InjectDataSource()\n    private readonly dataSource: DataSource,\n    @Inject(OutboxPublisher)\n    private readonly outboxPublisher: TenantErasureOutboxPublisher,\n    @Inject(LegalHoldService)\n    private readonly legalHoldService: TenantErasureLegalHoldService,\n    @Inject(ScheduledJobRunner) readonly scheduledJobs: ScheduledJobExecutor,\n  ) {}\n\n  async onModuleInit(): Promise<void> {\n    for (const targetService of TENANT_ERASURE_TARGET_SERVICES) {\n      for (const outcome of TENANT_ERASURE_OUTCOME_KINDS) {\n        await this.eventBus.subscribeWildcard(\n          TENANT_ERASURE_OUTCOME_EVENT_TYPES_BY_TARGET[targetService][outcome],\n          this,\n        );\n      }\n    }\n    this.logger.log(\n      'Subscribed to certificate-bound tenant erasure outcome events for finalization',\n    );\n  }\n\n  getEventType(): string {\n    return 'TenantErasureProof';\n  }\n\n  async handle(event: ErasureProofEvent): Promise<HandlerOutcome> {\n    const resolved = resolveTenantErasureOutcomeEventType(event.eventType);\n    if (!resolved) {\n      // PLAT-HIGH-902: a legacy/unknown outcome shape can never be recorded —\n      // dead-letter it instead of redelivering it until the budget is spent.\n      return HandlerOutcome.terminate(\n        `Unknown or legacy tenant-erasure outcome event type: ${event.eventType}`,\n      );\n    }\n    const claimedService =\n      resolved.outcome === 'blocked'\n        ? (event as TenantErasureBlockedEvent).blockedByService\n        : (event as TenantDataErasedEvent | TenantDataErasureFailedEvent).targetService;\n    if (claimedService !== resolved.targetService) {\n      return HandlerOutcome.terminate(\n        `Tenant-erasure outcome identity mismatch: eventType ${event.eventType} ` +\n          `is bound to ${resolved.targetService}, payload claims ${claimedService}`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    if (resolved.outcome === 'erased') {\n      await this.recordServiceProof(event as TenantDataErasedEvent);\n      return HandlerOutcome.ack();\n    }\n    await this.recordServiceFailure(\n      event as TenantDataErasureFailedEvent | TenantErasureBlockedEvent,\n      resolved.outcome,\n    );\n    return HandlerOutcome.ack();\n  }\n\n  @ScheduledJob({ name: 'tenant-erasure.poll-schema-deletion', every: 30_000 })\n  async pollSchemaDeletionCompletion(): Promise<void> {\n    const operations = queryRowsNormalized<{ id: string; tenantId: string }>(\n      await this.dataSource.query(\n        `SELECT id, \"tenantId\"\n           FROM admin.tenant_erasure_operations\n          WHERE status = 'IN_PROGRESS'\n            AND \"schemaDeletionJobId\" IS NOT NULL\n          ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" ASC\n          LIMIT $1`,\n        [TenantErasureProofHandler.SCHEMA_DELETION_POLL_LIMIT],\n      ),\n    );\n\n    for (const row of operations) {\n      await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n        const operation = await this.loadOperationForUpdate(manager, row.id, row.tenantId);\n        if (operation.status !== 'IN_PROGRESS') {\n          return;\n        }\n        const proofs = this.asRecord(operation.proofs);\n        if (!this.hasEveryTargetProof(operation, proofs)) {\n          return;\n        }\n        this.assertProofModes(operation, proofs);\n        await this.advanceAfterTargetProofs(\n          manager,\n          operation,\n          proofs,\n          this.extractCausationEventId(operation, proofs),\n        );\n      });\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Replays requests whose original outbox delivery never produced every\n   * target proof. The row lock makes the claim safe across replicas; the\n   * heartbeat moves only after the replacement outbox row is durable in the\n   * same transaction, so a failed enqueue remains immediately recoverable.\n   */\n  @ScheduledJob({ name: 'tenant-erasure.recover-stale-requests', every: 30_000 })\n  async recoverStaleErasureRequests(): Promise<void> {\n    await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n      const operations = queryRowsNormalized<TenantErasureRecoveryRow>(\n        await manager.query(\n          `SELECT id,\n                  \"tenantId\",\n                  \"requestedBy\",\n                  \"requestedAt\",\n                  \"legalHoldCheckedAt\",\n                  \"dryRun\",\n                  \"targetServices\",\n                  \"updatedAt\"\n             FROM admin.tenant_erasure_operations AS operation\n            WHERE operation.status = 'IN_PROGRESS'\n              AND operation.\"schemaDeletionJobId\" IS NULL\n              AND operation.\"updatedAt\" <=\n                    NOW() - ($2::double precision * INTERVAL '1 second')\n              AND EXISTS (\n                SELECT 1\n                  FROM unnest(operation.\"targetServices\") AS target(service)\n                 WHERE NOT (operation.proofs ? target.service)\n              )\n            ORDER BY operation.\"updatedAt\" ASC, operation.id ASC\n            LIMIT $1\n            FOR UPDATE OF operation SKIP LOCKED`,\n          [\n            TenantErasureProofHandler.REQUEST_RECOVERY_LIMIT,\n            TENANT_ERASURE_REQUEST_RECOVERY_STALE_SECONDS,\n          ],\n        ),\n      );\n\n      for (const operation of operations) {\n        if (typeof operation.dryRun !== 'boolean' || operation.targetServices.length === 0) {\n          throw new Error(\n            `Tenant erasure operation ${operation.id} has invalid durable request metadata`,\n          );\n        }\n        const recoveryGeneration = this.toIso(operation.updatedAt);\n        const event: TenantErasureRequestedEvent = {\n          ...createBaseEvent<TenantErasureRequestedEvent>(\n            'TenantErasureRequested',\n            operation.tenantId,\n            {\n              aggregateId: operation.tenantId,\n              aggregateType: 'Tenant',\n              userId: operation.requestedBy,\n            },\n          ),\n          operationId: operation.id,\n          requestedBy: operation.requestedBy,\n          requestedAt: this.toIso(operation.requestedAt),\n          legalHoldCheckedAt: this.toIso(operation.legalHoldCheckedAt),\n          dryRun: operation.dryRun,\n          targetServiceCount: operation.targetServices.length,\n        };\n        await this.outboxPublisher.enqueue(event, manager, {\n          aggregateId: operation.tenantId,\n          idempotencyKey: `tenant-erasure:${operation.id}:recovery:${recoveryGeneration}`,\n        });\n        await manager.query(\n          `UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations\n              SET \"updatedAt\" = NOW()\n            WHERE id = $1`,\n          [operation.id],\n        );\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  private async recordServiceProof(event: TenantDataErasedEvent): Promise<void> {\n    if (!isTenantErasureTargetService(event.targetService)) {\n      throw new BadRequestException(\n        `Unknown tenant-erasure target service: ${event.targetService}`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n      const operation = await this.loadOperationForUpdate(\n        manager,\n        event.operationId,\n        event.tenantId,\n      );\n      if (operation.status === 'COMPLETED') {\n        this.logger.warn(\n          `Ignoring replayed TenantDataErased for completed operation ${event.operationId}`,\n        );\n        return;\n      }\n      if (operation.status !== 'IN_PROGRESS') {\n        throw new BadRequestException(\n          `Tenant erasure operation ${event.operationId} is ${operation.status}; cannot accept proof.`,\n        );\n      }\n      if (event.dryRun !== operation.dryRun) {\n        throw new BadRequestException(\n          `Tenant erasure operation ${event.operationId} mode mismatch: ` +\n            `expected dryRun=${operation.dryRun}, received dryRun=${event.dryRun}.`,\n        );\n      }\n\n      const proofs = this.asRecord(operation.proofs);\n      proofs[event.targetService] = {\n        targetService: event.targetService,\n        erasedAt: event.erasedAt,\n        dryRun: event.dryRun,\n        matchedRecordCount: event.matchedRecordCount,\n        erasedRecordCount: event.erasedRecordCount,\n        proofHash: event.proofHash,\n        eventId: event.eventId,\n      };\n      this.assertProofModes(operation, proofs);\n\n      if (!this.hasEveryTargetProof(operation, proofs)) {\n        await this.updateOperationProgress(manager, operation.id, proofs);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      await this.advanceAfterTargetProofs(manager, operation, proofs, event.eventId);\n    });\n  }\n\n  private async recordServiceFailure(\n    event: TenantDataErasureFailedEvent | TenantErasureBlockedEvent,\n    outcome: 'failed' | 'blocked',\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    const targetService =\n      outcome === 'failed'\n        ? (event as TenantDataErasureFailedEvent).targetService\n        : (event as TenantErasureBlockedEvent).blockedByService;\n    if (targetService !== 'platform-orchestrator' && !isTenantErasureTargetService(targetService)) {\n      throw new BadRequestException(`Unknown tenant-erasure target service: ${targetService}`);\n    }\n\n    await this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => {\n      const operation = await this.loadOperationForUpdate(\n        manager,\n        event.operationId,\n        event.tenantId,\n      );\n      if (operation.status === 'COMPLETED') {\n        throw new BadRequestException(\n          `Tenant erasure operation ${event.operationId} is already completed.`,\n        );\n      }\n\n      const failures = Array.isArray(operation.failures) ? [...operation.failures] : [];\n      failures.push({\n        eventType: event.eventType,\n        targetService,\n        reason:\n          outcome === 'failed'\n            ? (event as TenantDataErasureFailedEvent).errorMessage\n            : (event as TenantErasureBlockedEvent).reason,\n        occurredAt:\n          outcome === 'failed'\n            ? (event as TenantDataErasureFailedEvent).failedAt\n            : (event as TenantErasureBlockedEvent).blockedAt,\n        eventId: event.eventId,\n      });\n\n      await manager.query(\n        `UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations\n            SET status = $2,\n                failures = $3::jsonb,\n                \"updatedAt\" = NOW()\n          WHERE id = $1`,\n        [operation.id, outcome === 'blocked' ? 'BLOCKED' : 'FAILED', JSON.stringify(failures)],\n      );\n    });\n  }\n\n  private async advanceAfterTargetProofs(\n    manager: EntityManager,\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n    proofs: Record<string, unknown>,\n    causationEventId: string,\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    if (operation.dryRun) {\n      if (operation.schemaDeletionJobId) {\n        await this.recordDryRunSchemaDeletionContamination(manager, operation);\n        return;\n      }\n      await this.completeDryRun(manager, operation, proofs);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const schemaDeletion = !operation.schemaDeletionJobId\n      ? await this.requestSchemaDeletion(manager, operation, proofs)\n      : await this.readSchemaDeletionState(manager, operation);\n\n    if (schemaDeletion.jobStatus === 'FAILED' || schemaDeletion.jobStatus === 'ABORTED') {\n      await this.recordSchemaDeletionFailure(manager, operation, schemaDeletion);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (!this.isSchemaDeletionComplete(schemaDeletion)) {\n      await this.updateOperationProgress(manager, operation.id, proofs);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    await this.finalizeOperation(manager, operation, proofs, causationEventId, schemaDeletion);\n  }\n\n  private assertProofModes(\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n    proofs: Record<string, unknown>,\n  ): void {\n    for (const targetService of operation.targetServices) {\n      if (proofs[targetService] === undefined) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      const proof = this.asRecord(proofs[targetService]);\n      if (proof['dryRun'] !== operation.dryRun) {\n        throw new BadRequestException(\n          `Tenant erasure operation ${operation.id} has a ${targetService} proof ` +\n            `whose dryRun mode does not match the durable operation.`,\n        );\n      }\n      if (operation.dryRun && proof['erasedRecordCount'] !== 0) {\n        throw new BadRequestException(\n          `Tenant erasure dry run ${operation.id} has a destructive ${targetService} proof ` +\n            'with a non-zero erasedRecordCount.',\n        );\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  private async recordDryRunSchemaDeletionContamination(\n    manager: EntityManager,\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    const failures = Array.isArray(operation.failures) ? [...operation.failures] : [];\n    failures.push({\n      eventType: 'TenantErasureDryRunSchemaDeletionRejected',\n      targetService: 'platform-orchestrator',\n      jobId: operation.schemaDeletionJobId,\n      reason: 'Dry-run operation contains a schema deletion job and cannot be completed safely',\n      occurredAt: new Date().toISOString(),\n    });\n    await manager.query(\n      `UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations\n          SET status = 'FAILED',\n              failures = $2::jsonb,\n              \"updatedAt\" = NOW()\n        WHERE id = $1`,\n      [operation.id, JSON.stringify(failures)],\n    );\n  }\n\n  private async completeDryRun(\n    manager: EntityManager,\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n    proofs: Record<string, unknown>,\n  ): Promise<void> {\n    const completedAt = new Date().toISOString();\n    const targetProofs = operation.targetServices.map((targetService) => ({\n      targetService,\n      proof: proofs[targetService],\n    }));\n    const proofHash = `sha256:${createHash('sha256')\n      .update(\n        this.stableStringify({\n          operationId: operation.id,\n          tenantId: operation.tenantId,\n          mode: 'DRY_RUN',\n          requestedAt: this.toIso(operation.requestedAt),\n          legalHoldCheckedAt: this.toIso(operation.legalHoldCheckedAt),\n          completedAt,\n          targetProofs,\n          proofVersion: 1,\n        }),\n      )\n      .digest('hex')}`;\n\n    await manager.query(\n      `UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations\n          SET status = 'COMPLETED',\n              proofs = $2::jsonb,\n              \"proofHash\" = $3,\n              \"completedAt\" = $4,\n              \"updatedAt\" = NOW()\n        WHERE id = $1`,\n      [operation.id, JSON.stringify(proofs), proofHash, completedAt],\n    );\n  }\n\n  private hasEveryTargetProof(\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n    proofs: Record<string, unknown>,\n  ): boolean {\n    return operation.targetServices.every((service) => proofs[service] !== undefined);\n  }\n\n  private async requestSchemaDeletion(\n    manager: EntityManager,\n    operation: TenantErasureOperationRow,\n    proofs: Record<string, unknown>,\n  ): Promise<TenantSchemaDeletionState> {\n    const schemaRow = await this.loadTenantSchemaForUpdate(manager, operation.tenantId);\n    const existingSchemas = await this.readExistingTenantSchemas(manager, [schemaRow.schemaName]);\n    const requestedAt = new Date().toISOString();\n    const legalHoldCheckedAt = await this.assertLiveLegalHold(operation.tenantId);\n    const proof = createCleanupDropProof({\n      operationId: operation.id,\n      tenantId: operation.tenantId,\n      purpose: 'tenant_erasure',\n      actorId: 'tenant-erasure-orchestrator',\n      reason: operation.reason,\n      legalHoldCheckedAt,\n      preCounts: {\n        schemaName: schemaRow.schemaName,\n        schemaLedgerStatus: schemaRow.status,\n        tableCount: schemaRow.tableCount,\n        existingSchemas,\n        initialLegalHoldCheckedAt: this.toIso(operation.legalHoldCheckedAt),\n        targetServices: operation.targetServices,\n        proofedTargets: Object.keys(proofs).sort(),\n      },\n    });\n\n    const rows = queryRowsNormalized<{ jobId: string }>(\n      await manager.query(\n        `SELECT platform.request_tenant_schema_deletion(\n           $1::uuid,\n           $2::uuid,\n           $3::text,\n           $4::jsonb\n         ) AS \"jobId\"`,\n        [\n          operation.id,\n          operation.tenantId,\n          schemaRow.schemaName,\n          JSON.stringify({\n            cleanupProof: proof,\n            tombstone: {\n              cleanupRunId: operation.id,\n              tenantId: operation.tenantId,\n              schemaName: schemaRow.schemaName,\n              requestedAt,\n              requestedBy: 'tenant-erasure-orchestrator',\n            },\n          }),\n        ],\n      ),\n    );","numLines":450,"startLine":250,"totalLines":1079}}}

\"confidence\": 0.88,\n      \"rationale\": \"What the rule guards and why it matters: a raw UPDATE against a table carrying a tenantId column, issued from code that knows the tenant, is a real defect when the row it addresses could belong to a different tenant. In that case a forged or mistaken operationId in an inbound erasure outcome event would let one tenant's event flip another tenant's erasure ledger row to BLOCKED or FAILED and append failures to it, corrupting GDPR erasure state across tenants in admin.tenant_erasure_operations. The correct shape is a write whose target row is bound to the tenant, either by a tenant column in the write's own predicate or by resolving the row through a tenant-checked, row-locked read in the same transaction. What the code actually does: lines 515 to 522 run UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations SET status = $2, failures = $3::jsonb, updatedAt = NOW() WHERE id = $1 with operation.id as $1 (line 521). That statement executes inside this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => ...) opened at line 488, and operation is the row returned at lines 489 to 493 by loadOperationForUpdate(manager, event.operationId, event.tenantId) on that same manager. loadOperationForUpdate (lines 952 to 987) selects FROM admin.tenant_erasure_operations WHERE id = $1 AND \\\"tenantId\\\" = $2 FOR UPDATE with parameters [operationId, tenantId] (lines 975, 976, 977), takes rows[0] (line 980), and throws NotFoundException when nothing matches (lines 981 to 985). So control reaches line 515 only when a row with exactly that id exists for exactly event.tenantId, and that row is locked for the rest of the transaction, which rules out a concurrent rebinding between the read and the write. The id is the operation UUID minted by randomUUID() at line 130 and inserted as the row id at line 165 onward; the service's CreateTenantErasureOperations migration declares it uuid PRIMARY KEY (consulted only to calibrate uniqueness; it is not among the request's admissible refs, so it is not cited). A primary-key predicate addresses at most one row, and that one row is the tenant-verified, locked row. Why this contradicts the finding: the tenant predicate is explicit, executed in the same transaction, on the same row identity the write then uses; the write at line 515 is a keyed follow-up to a tenant-scoped locked read, not a tenant-blind query. A forged event.operationId belonging to another tenant fails at line 982 before any write. The identical load-then-update-by-primary-key convention is used by every other write in this handler (lines 414, 594, 629, 707, 867, 931, 994), and the table lives in the admin control-plane schema, which admin-api-service operates across all tenants by design. Downstream surface: the admin erasure ledger and the TenantErasure outcome flow; no cross-tenant write path exists through line 515, so no code change is warranted from this finding. Evidence handling: the request excerpt covered lines 1 to 251, which does not include line 515, so I read the file at the worktree snapshot; the excerpt content for lines 1 to 251 matched what I read. Residual uncertainty behind the 0.88: if the operator rubric for this rule labels any raw write lacking its own tenant column as positive on defense-in-depth policy grounds regardless of a same-transaction guard, the finding would be a policy hit rather than a behavioral defect; I judge behavior, and the behavior is tenant-safe.\",\n      \"evidence_refs\": [\n \"confidence\": 0.88,\n      \"rationale\": \"What the rule guards and why it matters: a raw UPDATE against a table carrying a tenantId column, issued from code that knows the tenant, is a real defect when the row it addresses could belong to a different tenant. In that case a forged or mistaken operationId in an inbound erasure outcome event would let one tenant's event flip another tenant's erasure ledger row to BLOCKED or FAILED and append failures to it, corrupting GDPR erasure state across tenants in admin.tenant_erasure_operations. The correct shape is a write whose target row is bound to the tenant, either by a tenant column in the write's own predicate or by resolving the row through a tenant-checked, row-locked read in the same transaction. What the code actually does: lines 515 to 522 run UPDATE admin.tenant_erasure_operations SET status = $2, failures = $3::jsonb, updatedAt = NOW() WHERE id = $1 with operation.id as $1 (line 521). That statement executes inside this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => ...) opened at line 488, and operation is the row returned at lines 489 to 493 by loadOperationForUpdate(manager, event.operationId, event.tenantId) on that same manager. loadOperationForUpdate (lines 952 to 987) selects FROM admin.tenant_erasure_operations WHERE id = $1 AND \\\"tenantId\\\" = $2 FOR UPDATE with parameters [operationId, tenantId] (lines 975, 976, 977), takes rows[0] (line 980), and throws NotFoundException when nothing matches (lines 981 to 985). So control reaches line 515 only when a row with exactly that id exists for exactly event.tenantId, and that row is locked for the rest of the transaction, which rules out a concurrent rebinding between the read and the write. The id is the operation UUID minted by randomUUID() at line 130 and inserted as the row id at line 165 onward; the service's CreateTenantErasureOperations migration declares it uuid PRIMARY KEY (consulted only to calibrate uniqueness; it is not among the request's admissible refs, so it is not cited). A primary-key predicate addresses at most one row, and that one row is the tenant-verified, locked row. Why this contradicts the finding: the tenant predicate is explicit, executed in the same transaction, on the same row identity the write then uses; the write at line 515 is a keyed follow-up to a tenant-scoped locked read, not a tenant-blind query. A forged event.operationId belonging to another tenant fails at line 982 before any write. The identical load-then-update-by-primary-key convention is used by every other write in this handler (lines 414, 594, 629, 707, 867, 931, 994), and the table lives in the admin control-plane schema, which admin-api-service operates across all tenants by design. Downstream surface: the admin erasure ledger and the TenantErasure outcome flow; no cross-tenant write path exists through line 515, so no code change is warranted from this finding. Evidence handling: the request excerpt covered lines 1 to 251, which does not include line 515, so I read the file at the worktree snapshot; the excerpt content for lines 1 to 251 matched what I read. Residual uncertainty behind the 0.88: if the operator rubric for this rule labels any raw write lacking its own tenant column as positive on defense-in-depth policy grounds regardless of a same-transaction guard, the finding would be a policy hit rather than a behavioral defect; I judge behavior, and the behavior is tenant-safe.\",\n      \"evidence_refs\": [\n
